claims.text: The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a quasi-static yield strength of 786 MPa, compressive strength of 1314 MPa, and fracture strain of 13.5%.
The baseline HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has a single-phase microstructure typical of refractory high-entropy alloys.
Nb is a low-stacking-fault-energy microalloying element suitable for lowering the stacking-fault energy of HfZrTiTa0.53.
Adding a modest amount of Nb to HfZrTiTa0.53 will promote nanoscale twin nucleation during high-strain-rate deformation.
The microalloy-induced nanoscale twins will remain stable under high-strain-rate conditions.
Lowering stacking-fault energy lowers the energy barrier for twin formation.
Nanoscale twins act as barriers to dislocation motion.
The twins help distribute local deformation and thereby delay strain localization.
Adiabatic heating competes with and can deter twin-associated strain hardening under high-rate loading.
Nb-microalloyed HfZrTiTa0.53 will have dynamic yield and compressive strengths approximately 10–20% higher than the baseline.
Nb-microalloyed HfZrTiTa0.53 will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate than the baseline.
Nb-microalloyed HfZrTiTa0.53 will exhibit greater uniform deformation and a higher effective fracture strain than the baseline.
Nb-microalloyed HfZrTiTa0.53 will resist strain localization and fail later than the baseline.
Nb microalloying will produce a more gradual stress decline and moderate the rapid release of impact energy.
The unmodified HfZrTiTa0.53 alloy has limited strain hardening, poor uniform deformability, and rapid failure with sharp energy release under adiabatic dynamic loading.
The predicted improvement applies under impact loading at strain rates around 10^3 s^-1 where adiabatic heating is significant.
The beneficial effect will be less pronounced under quasi-static or cryogenic conditions.
